newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Gov. says $425 mln stadium measure passes.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Gov. says $425 mln stadium measure passes.

text.p: Washington's governor made it official Thursday, declaring the passage of a $425 million football stadium measure.

Gov. Gary Locke said the stadium measure was passed by a margin of 36,780 votes, with 51 percent in favor and 49 percent opposed. The vote was certified more than a week after the state's special stadium election.
"The people have saved professional football for the state of Washington," Locke said.
The heated stadium election pit well-funded supporters, backed by billionaire Paul Allen, against cash-strapped opponents who recruited consumer activist Ralph Nader.

The measure will provide $325 million in public money for a 72,000-seat open-air stadium to house the Seattle Seahawks. Allen, co-founder of Microsoft Corp and owner of the NBA Portland Trail Blazers, will invest an additional $100 million in the project.

Allen, worth more than $13 billion, offered to buy the Seahawks -- but only if the stadium referendum was approved. The new stadium will replace the aging Kingdome, an indoor facility that would be demolished.

The stadium financing package includes $101 million from existing sales taxes, $127 million from lottery games, $56 million in stadium admissions and parking taxes, and $40 million in hotel room taxes.
The state will issue up to $300 million of bonds to pay for site acquisition, design and construction of the stadium and an exhibition center.
